program: P1.7 Reality Repair Sprint — Phase 4: Operational Drift Detection

data_window.data_source: REAL DATA ONLY — no interpolation, no synthetic augmentation

segment_definitions.method: UTC-based segmentation aligned with circadian_attention_report.json periods

2026-05-11_sun.notes: Bootstrap day. System started mid-day. Both real incidents occurred. 8-hour gap (13:36-21:49). Dense burst activity during incidents.

2026-05-12_mon.notes: System was idle/offline for entirety of Monday. 38-hour gap from 2026-05-11T22:14 to 2026-05-13T12:25.

2026-05-13_tue.notes: System restarted at 12:25 UTC. night35-dmn-tick daemon activated ~15:00 UTC, achieving 60s cadence. Governance framework tests generated most anomalies (skillify pipeline). No real incidents.

2026-05-14_wed.notes: Continuous 60s DMN tick sampling throughout. Highest event density of any day due to stable daemon operation. No incidents.

signal_density_drift.description: Signal density evolved dramatically across the observation window

phases.pattern: Burst initialization — 19 telemetry snapshots in 8 seconds, then sporadic setup activity
ZERO events — system was running but not instrumented. This is the critical GAP-001.
Extreme burst — 337 events in 25 minutes during incident detection, health scoring, reflex triggers, and diagnostics
ZERO events — system offline/idle. Unrecoverable gap (GAP-002).
System restart. Agent-driven setup, governance tests, manual operations.
Stable 60s DMN tick cadence. 3 actions per tick cycle (~20s effective interval). This is the target operational mode.

signal_density_drift.drift_verdict: STRONG POSITIVE DRIFT — system evolved from 0 events/hour to 360 events/hour steady-state. The transition from ad-hoc to daemon-driven telemetry is the single most significant operational improvement.

day_vs_night_analysis.methodology: Analyzed only the daemon-stable period (May 13 15:00 - May 14 06:16 UTC) to measure true circadian variation in signal density

daytime_utc_0900_1800.notes: Limited daytime data in daemon-stable period (only May 13 15:00-18:00 UTC)

nighttime_utc_0000_0600.notes: Daemon maintains consistent cadence through night. Zero anomalies in stable nighttime operation.

late_night_utc_2100_0000.notes: Post-daemon late_night shows zero anomalies — unlike May 11 late_night which had both incidents. Insufficient data to determine if May 11 incidents were situational or circadian.

day_vs_night_analysis.conclusion: Once daemon is stable, signal density is constant across day/night — the 60s tick eliminates observability gaps. Anomaly density varies by period but insufficient daemon-era data to establish circadian anomaly patterns.

weekend_data.notes: Weekend data is from bootstrap day — not representative of normal weekend operation

weekday_data.notes: Weekday data includes daemon-stable period. Higher event density is due to daemon activation, not weekday effect.

weekday_vs_weekend.conclusion: INCONCLUSIVE — weekend vs weekday comparison is confounded by system evolution (bootstrap vs daemon-stable). Cannot attribute event density differences to day-of-week patterns. Need 2+ complete weeks of daemon-stable operation.

quiet_period_analysis.definition: Periods with zero events or event rate < 1/hour

quiet_periods_detected.type: PRE_DAEMON — system running but not instrumented

quiet_period_analysis.conclusion: Zero quiet periods since daemon activation (May 13 ~15:00). The 60s tick cadence eliminates observability quiet periods entirely. Pre-daemon era had two major quiet periods (8h + 38h) that are the primary data quality blockers.

operator_presence_indicators.methodology: Inferred from action types: cursor-agent actions, governance tests, manual commands indicate operator presence

detected_sessions.indicator: Bootstrap actions, sense_local, vision_capture — initial setup
Automated incident response — no human operator detected, pure reflex
cursor-agent driven: governance framework build, tests, skillify pipeline. Operator actively developing.
Autonomous daemon only — no operator-initiated actions. Pure autonomous operation.

operator_presence_indicators.conclusion: Clear operator presence during daytime (UTC+8 evening/night), autonomous operation during UTC nighttime (local daytime). The system shows two operational modes: supervised development and autonomous daemon.

detected.description: System restart after 38-hour gap. Agent-driven setup, daemon activation.

deployment_maintenance_windows.conclusion: Two deployment windows detected. Both were operator-initiated. No automated maintenance windows observed.

quiet_hours_0000_0600.notes: Dominated by daemon-era data (May 14 00:00-06:16). High event density from 60s tick cadence. Anomalies are from governance tests, not real incidents.

transition_morning_0600_0900.notes: Sparse data. Only available from May 13 transition. Low activity.

active_hours_0900_1800.notes: Includes 8.2-hour gap (May 11 13:37-21:49). Post-daemon active hours have ~360 events/hour.

transition_evening_1800_2100.notes: Clean operations. No anomalies detected. Moderate event density.

late_night_2100_0000.notes: Includes the May 11 incident burst (790 events/hour). Post-daemon late_night (May 13) was calm (360 events/hour, 0 anomalies). Anomaly density is dominated by the single incident day.

drift_summary.primary_drift_pattern: POSITIVE — system evolved from sparse ad-hoc telemetry to continuous 60s daemon-driven sampling
drift_summary.key_inflection_point: 2026-05-13T15:00 UTC — daemon activation. Before this: coverage_ratio ≈ 0.19. After this: coverage_ratio ≈ 1.00 (continuous).
drift_summary.circadian_drift_confidence: LOW — only ~15 hours of daemon-stable data across 2 circadian periods. Cannot establish circadian drift patterns yet.
